I am 48 years old and have been farming these 9.2 mu in Quzhou for twenty years. With only my wife and me working the land, I know I cannot chase every crop. I stick to what feeds us and what the buyers at the county market always take.

This year I will manage my land the same way I always have. My backbone is the cabbage–chinese cabbage–spinach rotation, and I will keep a small piece of land for summer vegetables so we have cash coming in at different times of the year.

I will put **2.5 mu into spring cabbage** starting in March. I buy hybrid seeds from the county seed station because the heads are tight and heavy, and they resist the soft-rot that used to ruin my crop. I will rotary-till the soil deep, spread compound fertilizer as a base, and top-dress with urea twice. From my well I will irrigate five times, especially when the heads are forming, and I will spray four times for caterpillars and aphids.

For **autumn chinese cabbage** I will plant **3 mu** in late July. This is my biggest plot because the price is steady in autumn and it stores well if the market drops. Again I use hybrid seeds, rotary tillage, and four irrigations. It needs three sprays—less than spring cabbage because the autumn pests are milder here.

**Spinach** will take **2 mu**. I sow it in October so it overwinters and comes up early next spring. I use improved seeds, not hybrid, because hybrid spinach seed is too expensive for a crop that grows so fast. It needs lighter fertilizer and only two sprays. I will water it three times, mostly in spring when the weather turns dry.

The remaining **1.2 mu** I will use for summer cash crops: **0.8 mu chili**, **0.5 mu eggplant**, and **0.4 mu kidney bean**. Wait, I need to check my math—0.8 + 0.5 + 0.4 is 1.7, which is too much. I only have 1.2 mu left. Let me fix that. I will plant **0.6 mu chili**, **0.4 mu eggplant**, and **0.2 mu kidney bean** along the edge of the chili plot. That makes exactly 1.2 mu. For chili and eggplant I buy hybrid seeds because they bear longer and the fruits look better. Kidney beans I plant with improved seeds I saved from last year. These summer crops need more heat and water, so I will irrigate four to five times from the well and spray three to five times depending on what insects show up.

I rotary-till every plot because our soil gets hard as brick after the winter. I have learned over twenty years that if the roots cannot breathe, the yield drops no matter how much fertilizer you throw on.
